clue.text: Face endless people giving a stream of abuse

indicators.note: something without an end has lost its final letter, so the word for face is cut short

blocks.note: a dial is the face of a clock or watch
a tribe is a people or clan

explanation.surface: Someone confronting an endless crowd of people who are shouting insults at them.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter verbal attack, a torrent of abusive criticism.

clue.text: Overshadows front of dry docks, we hear

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter only
what we hear is spoken, so the spelling follows the sound rather than the meaning

blocks.note: opening letter of dry
wharfs are docks; said out loud they match this spelling

explanation.surface: Someone notices that a dry dock seems to tower over things.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwarf something is to make it look small by comparison, i.e. to tower over it.

clue.text: Canadian showman and artist in capital

blocks.note: Paul Anka is a Canadian singer and entertainer
RA is a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: A Canadian entertainer and a painter turn up together in a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Ankara is the capital city of Turkey.

clue.text: Fellow lodgers are most fussy about order

indicators.note: fussy suggests fiddling about, so the letters are fiddled into a new arrangement
about means around, so the rearranged letters go round the other piece

blocks.note: the letters taken as written
OM is the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: People sharing lodgings are the most fussy about keeping things tidy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like tidiness but is the British honour, the Order of Merit.
explanation.definitionFit: Roommates are people who share a room or lodging, i.e. fellow lodgers.

clue.text: Sherry and port, the best

blocks.note: Bristol is a port city in south-west England
the cream is the best part

explanation.surface: Sherry and port are named the best fortified wines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the wine alongside sherry, but it is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Harveys Bristol Cream is a well-known brand of sweet cream sherry.

clue.text: Locksmith?

blocks.note: surface reading: a tradesman who makes and repairs locks for doors
setter's reading: someone who works on locks of hair, cutting them for a living

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark warns that 'lock' is not the door kind: a lock is also a tress of hair, and a smith is a worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's hairdresser trims locks of hair, so he is playfully a smith of locks.

clue.text: A help in translation of a letter in Hebrew

indicators.note: translating turns words into a different form, so these letters take a new order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A translation aid for reading a letter written in Hebrew.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleph is the first letter of the Hebrew alphabet.

clue.text: Bonnet and boot

blocks.note: first meaning: a flat Scottish brimless cap
second meaning: a heavy laced walking boot

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bonnet and boot' suggests the front and back of a car; both are items of clothing named after the royal estate in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a Scottish cap and a style of laced boot take their name from the royal castle in Aberdeenshire.

clue.text: Aide-memoire concerning bodyguard

blocks.note: re means concerning
a minder is a bodyguard

explanation.surface: A memo note about someone's personal protection officer.
explanation.definitionFit: An aide-memoire is a note to jog the memory, which is what a reminder does.

clue.text: Request to see Italian and invite trouble

blocks.note: to ask for someone is to request to see them
IT is the standard abbreviation for Italian

explanation.surface: Asking to meet an Italian is presented as a way of courting trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To ask for it is an idiom for behaving so as to provoke the trouble that follows.

clue.text: Plot to strike causes a state of uproar

blocks.note: a plot of garden ground, as in a flower bed
to lam is an informal verb for to beat or thrash

explanation.surface: A plan for an industrial strike that throws everything into chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' suggests a conspiracy, but it is a patch of garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedlam, named from a London madhouse, means scenes of wild noisy confusion.

clue.text: US actor/director's 1988 British film Kate worked on

indicators.note: worked means kneaded or shaped, so the letters are reshaped

blocks.note: Buster is a 1988 British film starring Phil Collins
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An American filmmaker's 1988 British picture that an actress called Kate worked on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worked on' looks like one phrase, but 'on' is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Buster Keaton was an American silent-film comedian who also directed his films.

clue.text: Drink after Foreign Office meeting

indicators.note: following tells us the drink is placed behind the department's initials

blocks.note: FO is the abbreviation for the Foreign Office
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: Diplomats have a drink once their Foreign Office meeting is over.
explanation.walkthrough: The Foreign Office is the British government department for overseas affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A forum is an assembly or gathering for public discussion of issues.

clue.text: Try to land

blocks.note: first meaning: a score in American football, akin to a rugby try
second meaning: an aircraft's arrival on the runway

explanation.walkthrough: 'Try to land' reads like an attempt at landing; split it into a scoring term and a noun for an aircraft landing.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby a try is grounding the ball, also called a touchdown, and a plane's landing is its touchdown.

clue.text: High tea - treat a lad, but not now

indicators.note: high can mean intoxicated, and an addled state scrambles the order of what follows

blocks.note: the twelve letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone promises a boy a high tea as a treat, but just not today.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High tea' looks like a single phrase, a British early-evening meal, but 'High' is detached as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: At a later date means at some future time, i.e. postponed rather than happening now.

clue.text: Self-control shown by others surrounding coach

indicators.note: surrounding means going all round, so one word encloses the other

blocks.note: the rest means the others
to coach is to train

explanation.surface: The other players show composure around their coach.
explanation.definitionFit: Restraint is holding oneself back, the exercise of self-control.

clue.text: Frank's flat

blocks.note: first meaning: honest and direct
second meaning: level, without curves

explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank's flat' reads as a man's apartment; both words are adjectives.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight describes a candid, honest person and also a line or surface with no bends.

clue.text: Carrying a gun as well, was first in court

blocks.note: too means as well
to have led is to have been first
to be up before a judge is to appear in court

explanation.surface: A defendant who was carrying a firearm too was first to appear before the court.
explanation.definitionFit: Tooled up is slang for armed, especially with a gun.

clue.text: Appropriate newspapers found in a hotel room, perhaps

definitions.text: found in a hotel room, perhaps
definitions.note: descriptive phrase standing for the thing

blocks.note: to trouser is slang for pocketing or appropriating money
the press means newspapers collectively

explanation.surface: A guest helps themself to newspapers lying about in a hotel room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' looks like the adjective meaning suitable but is the verb meaning to take.
explanation.definitionFit: A trouser press, a device for flattening trousers, is a typical fitting supplied in British hotel rooms.

clue.text: Wear nothing in port

indicators.note: in places the first item inside the second

blocks.note: a haven is a harbour
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Sailors going naked while in harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: To have something on is to be wearing it.

clue.text: Figure country must import uranium

indicators.note: to import is to bring inside, so one piece goes into the other

blocks.note: a state is a country
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A nation is obliged to bring in uranium, according to some figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' sounds like a number, but it is a sculpted form.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue is a sculpted figure of a person or animal.

clue.text: Level with complete stick-in-the-mud

blocks.note: all means whole or complete
a square is a conventional, old-fashioned person

explanation.surface: Someone is on equal terms with a thoroughly dull, conservative type.
explanation.definitionFit: All square means evenly matched, with scores tied, as in sport.

clue.text: Refer to short cut taken by tortoise at the end

indicators.note: short means lacking its final part, so the last letter is dropped
at the end points to the final letter of the word only

blocks.note: a cut is a share, a quota
final letter of tortoise

explanation.surface: Mentioning the tortoise that took a short cut to win the race at the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short cut' looks like a quicker route; read 'cut' as a share and 'short' as clipping it.
explanation.definitionFit: To quote a source is to cite or refer to it.

clue.text: Take it on before performance

indicators.note: placed ahead of tells us the first piece comes in front of the second

blocks.note: re means on or concerning
an act is a stage performance

explanation.surface: An actor agrees to take on a role ahead of the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take it on' looks like one phrase; split it after 'it', as in asking how someone took the news.
explanation.definitionFit: How someone takes something is how they respond to it, so to take it is to respond.

clue.text: I'd gone out for a Bible

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone explains they had gone out to fetch a Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: A Gideon is a Bible placed in hotel rooms by the Gideons International organisation.

clue.text: Small ballistic missile, shrill

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
Trident is a submarine-launched ballistic missile

explanation.surface: A little rocket that screams as it flies.
explanation.definitionFit: A strident voice or sound is loud, harsh and grating, much like a shrill one.

clue.text: Drunkard clutching soft hat

indicators.note: to clutch is to hold within one's grasp, so one word encloses the other

blocks.note: a toper is a habitual drinker
p is piano, the musical direction for soft

explanation.surface: A drunk clinging on to his floppy hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A topper is a top hat, a tall formal hat.

clue.text: Batting posture is a case in point

blocks.note: a cricket side batting is in
a stance is the way one stands

explanation.surface: A batsman's posture at the crease is offered as a typical example.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is an example of something, which is what a case in point is.
